entry.title: projectsend up to r1945 Auth.php ldap_email response discrepancy
entry.summary: A vulnerability was found in projectsend up to r1945 (Project Management Software). It has been rated as problematic. This issue affects some unknown processing of the file includes/Classes/Auth.php. There is no information about possible countermeasures known. It may be suggested to replace the affected object with an alternative product.

details.affected: A vulnerability was found in projectsend up to r1945 (Project Management Software). It has been rated as problematic.
details.vulnerability: The manipulation of the argument ldap_email with an unknown input leads to a unknown weakness. Using CWE to declare the problem leads to CWE-204. The product provides different responses to incoming requests in a way that reveals internal state information to an unauthorized actor outside of the intended control sphere.
details.exploit: The exploit is available at drive.google.com. It is declared as proof-of-concept. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way. By approaching the search of inurl:includes/Classes/Auth.php it is possible to find vulnerable targets with Google Hacking.
details.countermeasure: There is no information about possible countermeasures known. It may be suggested to replace the affected object with an alternative product.

response.summary: The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

entry.title: OpenClaw up to 2026.2.17 File Existence tools.exec.safeBins information exposure
entry.summary: A vulnerability, which was classified as problematic, was found in OpenClaw up to 2026.2.17. Affected is the function tools.exec.safeBins of the component File Existence Handler. Upgrading to version 2026.2.19-beta.1 eliminates this vulnerability. The upgrade is hosted for download at github.com. Applying the patch bafdbb6f112409a65decd3d4e7350fbd637c7754 is able to eliminate this problem. The bugfix is ready for download at github.com. The best possible mitigation is suggested to be upgrading to the latest version.
